items.summary: WHO is seeking a consultant for 11 months to develop the Traditional Medicine (TM) code set of the International Classification of Health Interventions (ICHI), within the Classifications and Terminologies team, Department of Data, Digital Health, Analytics and AI. items.title: Influenza A(H5N1) - United States of America
items.summary: Between 16 October and 4 November 2026, the United States of America, through its International Health Regulations (IHR) National Focal Point, notified WHO of three laboratory-confirmed human infections with influenza A(H5) virus in Washington State. These included one fatal case, the first reported death following exposure to infected dairy cattle or a related contaminated environment. items.title: Countries face critical gaps in health inequality monitoring systems
items.summary: Health inequalities exist in every country. Yet millions of people at risk of being left behind may remain invisible in national health statistics. A new World Health Organization (WHO) report reveals that despite strong commitments, countries still face significant gaps in their ability to identify, measure and monitor health inequalities. items.title: WHO and China’s National Institutes for Drug Control sign agreement to strengthen access to quality-assured in vitro diagnostics
items.summary: On 2 September 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) and the National Institutes for Drug Control (NIDC) of the People’s Republic of China formally exchanged a signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on collaboration towards strengthening access to safe, quality-assured in vitro diagnostic medical devices.The signing marks an important step in WHO’s work to support countries in improving access to reliable diagnostics, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. items.title: Circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 1 – Syrian Arab Republic
items.summary: In October 2026, a cluster of four cases of acute flaccid paralysis (AFP) was identified in Al-Mayadin District, Deir Ez Zor Governorate, Syrian Arab Republic. As of 13 November 2026, three confirmed cases of circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 1 (cVDPV1) have been reported. Vaccine-derived poliovirus type 1 (VDPV1) was also detected in three contacts who did not present with AFP and are therefore not included in the reported paralytic poliomyelitis case count. items.title: Better medicines for every child: GAP-f partners accelerate action on World Children’s Day
items.summary: On World Children’s Day, the Global Accelerator for Paediatric Formulations Network (GAP-f) recognizes the progress being made towards ensuring that children benefit from medicines that are safe, effective and appropriate for their needs. Across the global health community, partners are working together to strengthen clinical research, advance the development of paediatric formulations and accelerate access to medicines. items.title: Every child deserves a healthy start and a healthy future
items.summary: Every child has the right to the highest attainable standard of health. Yet too many children are still being left behind. HIV, tuberculosis, viral hepatitis and syphilis continue to affect children worldwide, particularly where access to essential health services is limited.

items.title: Call for expressions of interest: Working Group on Community Health Worker Functions and Competencies in Health Emergencies
items.summary: To strengthen community-level preparedness and response, WHO is convening a working group to review and refine an existing draft framework describing CHW functions and competencies in emergencies. The review will consider different CHW profiles, a progressive, function-based approach and the conditions needed for safe implementation.

items.title: WHO publishes second edition of the Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel
items.summary: WHO has published the second edition of the Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, bringing together in a single document the Code adopted by the World Health Assembly in 2010 and the amendments adopted in May 2026. The new edition provides Member States and partners with an updated framework for managing the growing international mobility of health workers in ways that support stronger and more sustainable health systems. items.title: New WHO collaborating centre established to support work on foodborne disease burden
items.summary: WHO welcomes the Service Health Information, within the Epidemiology and Public Health Directorate at Sciensano, the Belgian scientific institute for human, animal and environmental health, based in Brussels, as the new WHO Collaborating Centre on Foodborne Disease Burden. The Centre will provide scientific and technical support to WHO’s work to measure and monitor the health and economic burden of foodborne diseases.

items.title: Chikungunya virus disease - Switzerland
items.summary: On 4 November 2026, health authorities in the canton of Ticino, Switzerland, in coordination with federal authorities, reported four locally acquired cases of chikungunya virus disease. These are the first reported locally acquired chikungunya cases in Switzerland. The earliest reported symptom onset was 10 August 2026, although this infection was identified retrospectively and the source of infection could not be identified. items.title: Governments make over 230 new pledges to prevent violence against children
items.summary: Governments are stepping up action to protect children from violence, with over 230 new pledges to be announced at the Second Global Ministerial Conference on Ending Violence Against Children in Manila, Philippines taking place on 18-19 November, the World Health Organization (WHO) said today. items.title: Leaders commit to accelerate action on obesity prevention and control
items.summary: Global health leaders, ministers and partners launched a new call for action today at the Global Obesity Summit in Spain, committing to accelerate progress in obesity prevention, early intervention and care.

items.title: Evidence mounts that exposure to hormone-disrupting chemicals starts before birth: UNEP–WHO report
items.summary: The State of the Science on Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals 2026 report, is the first major global update since the 2012 UNEP-WHO assessment; it finds that more than a decade of research has strengthened and broadened the evidence linking these chemicals with harm to people and wildlife.

items.title: Advocating for stronger, integrated cervical cancer prevention and care for women and girls living with HIV
items.summary: On World Cervical Cancer Elimination Day, WHO is calling for stronger integration of HIV and cervical cancer services to ensure that women and girls living with HIV receive timely prevention, screening, diagnosis and treatment of cervical cancer. A coordinated person-centred approach can reduce deaths, improve health outcomes and contribute to an improved quality of life. items.title: Countries expand cervical cancer screening and treatment, bringing elimination closer
items.summary: Three in five women aged 30–49 have never been screened for cervical cancer, according to new WHO estimates. Access to human papillomavirus (HPV) testing is particularly unequal. Only 2% of women in low- and middle-income countries were screened using HPV testing in the preceding five years, compared with 32% in high-income countries.

items.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS) – Qatar
items.summary: On 29 October 2026, the National International Health Regulations (IHR) Focal Point of the State of Qatar notified the World Health Organization (WHO) of two laboratory-confirmed cases of Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS). The cases were confirmed on 5 and 25 August 2026 and are the first MERS cases reported from Qatar since 2022. items.title: Yellow fever - WHO African Region
items.summary: Yellow fever transmission continues in the WHO African Region, with recent outbreak activity concentrated in parts of West Africa. Between 1 January and 12 October 2026, 67 confirmed cases, including 18 deaths, were recorded in nine countries in the Region: Burkina Faso, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria and Togo. items.title: Shamonda virus in human - France
items.summary: On 20 October 2026, the National IHR Focal Point (NFP) of France notified WHO regarding the first documented human infection with Shamonda virus (SHAV). The case was an immunocompromised older man from eastern France with no travel history during the preceding year. He developed severe neurological illness on 23 September 2026 and was diagnosed with severe encephalitis (brain inflammation). The patient died on 8 October 2026. items.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus - Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Between 1 January and 5 October 2026, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia reported eight laboratory-confirmed cases of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) infection, including one death. Cases were detected across six locations: Al Jouf (1), Arar (1), Hafr Al-Batin (1), Riyadh (2), Tabuk (1) and Taif (2). No epidemiological links were identified between any of the cases.
